capitals.name: Paris
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Paris'. The provisional government sat at Tours during the siege of 1870 ('Gambetta established the provisional republican government in the city of Tours') and, 'after the January 1871 surrender, ... a new seat of government at Versailles'; the page does not date the return to Paris (1879 in other sources, not opened).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1870: Cliopatria's Third Republic row begins in 1871 but the Republic dates from 4 September 1870, when 'the Second French Empire collapsed'. France was whole in law until the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871), so the 1870 shape is the 1873 shape plus Alsace-Lorraine (about 628,700 + 14,470 km2). The north-east was in German hands; that is the occupation and contest of the ledger, not a change of the shape.

correction.text: all of France on 4 September 1870, Alsace-Lorraine included

keyframe_review.note: 525,415 km2 for 1871-1872: the 1873 shape minus 451 cells (about 100,000 km2) in Marne, Aisne, Loiret, Pas-de-Calais, Aube, Meuse, Nord, Somme, Oise, Seine-et-Marne, Ardennes, Vosges, Eure-et-Loir, Meurthe-et-Moselle, Loir-et-Cher, Yonne, Haute-Marne and the Paris basin; the German Empire's Cliopatria shape of 1871-1872 carries exactly these cells. The treaty 'required military occupation in parts of France until the indemnity was paid' and the withdrawal 'occurred in September 1873': the land is French and occupied, hatched, not German; the page names no departments, so the zone is Cliopatria's. Alsace-Lorraine (ceded 10 May 1871) is correctly absent.

correction.text: France within the frontiers of 1873-1914 (metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine, with Corsica, the Savoy and Nice of 1860, French Guiana and the Antilles)

keyframe_review.note: 628,747 km2 for 1873-1914 against the infobox's 536,464 km2 for metropolitan France in 1894 (ratio 1.17): the shape also holds French Guiana (290 cells) and the Antilles, which account for the difference. Alsace-Lorraine is absent (annexed 1871). The shape's 'France' overlaps Suriname (8 cells) and Brazil's Amapa (3 cells) at French Guiana; not checked against a page.

602,699 km2: the 1873 shape minus 112 cells in Aisne, Nord, Ardennes, Somme, Pas-de-Calais, Meuse and Oise. 'The territory occupied by Germany held 64 percent of French pig-iron production' and 'Northeastern France fell under German occupation' (Third Republic page): land held by an army, not lost; the Republic kept its government in Paris. The correction is the 1873 shape and the occupation events carry the hatching.

correction.text: France within the frontiers of 1873-1914 (metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine, with Corsica, the Savoy and Nice of 1860, French Guiana and the Antilles)

keyframe_review.note: 602,104 km2: the 1915 shape (+3 cells, -7 in Pas-de-Calais, Meuse, Aisne: front-line noise). Same correction as 1915.

correction.text: France within the frontiers of 1873-1914 (metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine, with Corsica, the Savoy and Nice of 1860, French Guiana and the Antilles)

keyframe_review.note: 605,557 km2: the German withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line returns 11 cells in Oise, Somme and Aisne ('On 25 February the German armies west of the line began Operation Alberich ... completed on 5 April'), and 3 cells at Bitola (North Macedonia) appear: land of the Serbian state held by the Armee d'Orient, drawn as a contest. Correction: the 1873 shape, the Macedonian cells as a contest zone, the north-east as occupation.

correction.text: France within the frontiers of 1873-1914 (metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine, with Corsica, the Savoy and Nice of 1860, French Guiana and the Antilles)

keyframe_review.note: 605,272 km2: the 1917 shape minus 20 cells (Somme 5, Meuse 4, Aisne 2, Meurthe-et-Moselle 2, Oise 2, Marne 1: the German spring offensive of 1918 and the lines of November) plus the Vardar valley (Kavadartsi, Konce, Radovis, Gevgelija, Strumica, Dojran: 'the French and Serbians attacked and captured their objective' on 15 September 1918) and Beirut, Mount Lebanon and North Lebanon (French troops 'disembarked in Beirut' on 8 October). The Macedonian cells belong to Serbia and the Lebanese coast to the Ottoman Empire, then the mandate. Correction: the 1873 shape; those cells are ledger events.

correction.text: France within the frontiers of 1873-1914 (metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine, with Corsica, the Savoy and Nice of 1860, French Guiana and the Antilles)

keyframe_review.note: 673,774 km2 for 1919-1923: the 1873 shape plus Alsace-Lorraine ('France regained Alsace-Lorraine' by the Treaty of Versailles of 28 June 1919: Moselle 26, Bas-Rhin 18, Haut-Rhin 13 cells), the Rhineland (Rheinland-Pfalz 42 cells, Baden-Wurttemberg 2), the Saar (11 cells), Cilicia (Hatay 17, Adana 16, Osmaniye 6, Mersin 4, Gaziantep, Kilis) and the Lebanon coast and Aleppo/Idlib (about 16 cells). Only Alsace-Lorraine is French land. The Rhineland was occupied from 1 December 1918, Cilicia occupied until January 1922 and Lebanon/Syria a mandate from 1920; the Saar was under the League of Nations ('governed by the five-person Governing Commission'), not France.

correction.text: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine, as the frontier stood from 1919

keyframe_review.note: 661,398 km2 for 1924-1925: as 1919 without Cilicia and Lebanon (all gone by 1922) but with 21 more Rheinland-Pfalz cells (the French zone widened with the Ruhr/Koblenz take-over: 'On 27 January [1923], American General Allen officially handed over control to the French') and the Saar. Rhineland and Saar cells are occupation and League land. Correction: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine.

correction.text: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine, as the frontier stood from 1919

keyframe_review.note: 662,459 km2 for 1926-1929: as 1924 plus 5 North Rhine-Westphalia cells (cells at 6.5-7.1 E, 50.5-50.6 N; the British withdrew from the Cologne zone in January 1926 and the page does not say who took these cells, so the reading is uncertain). Rhineland cells are occupation (to 30 June 1930), not French land. Correction as 1924.

correction.text: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine, as the frontier stood from 1919

keyframe_review.note: 647,746 km2 for 1930-1931: the Rhineland cells are gone (the last troops 'withdrew from the Mainz zone on 30 June 1930', Koblenz evacuated in November 1929) but the Saar basin (Saarland 11 cells) remains in the shape; the territory 'was governed by the five-person Governing Commission' of the League of Nations from 10 January 1920 to 1 March 1935 ('Its coalfields were also to be ceded to France'). Correction: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine.

correction.text: France of 1873 plus Alsace-Lorraine, as the frontier stood from 1919

keyframe_review.note: 644,549 km2 for 1932-1935: the 1873 shape plus Alsace-Lorraine (628,747 + about 14,470 = 643,200 km2, ratio 1.00); the Saar is correctly absent (the plebiscite of 13 January 1935 was 90.8% for Germany, and the Reich took it back on 1 March 1935).
644,287 km2 for 1936-1937: same land; three cells of border noise. The Rhineland was 'occupied by the Wehrmacht in breach of the treaties on 7 March 1936' (Rhineland page); no frontier moves.
644,192 km2 for 1939: the last Cliopatria year; same land as 1938. The Battle of France follows in 1940 (new keyframe).

New keyframe 1940: Cliopatria has no shape after 1939. The Republic lasted 'until 10 July 1940, after the Fall of France' (Battle of France 10 May - 25 June 1940); the metropolis stays French in law, 'Nazi forces occupied much of France' and Vichy France is declared on 10 July. The occupation is a ledger event; the Vichy France row starts in 1940.

correction.text: France within its 1939 frontiers until the Republic ends on 10 July 1940, occupied in the north and west

ledger.note: 4 September 1870: the Third Republic is proclaimed in Paris. 'from 4 September 1870, when the Second French Empire collapsed during the Franco-Prussian War'; Favre, Gambetta and Trochu 'proclaimed a provisional government called the Government of National Defence' (Franco-Prussian War page), which sat at Tours during the siege of Paris.

region.text: all of France, Alsace-Lorraine included

ledger.note: September 1870: the republic continues the war. The German coalition 'invaded northeastern France on 4 August' and 'Prussian forces commenced the siege of Paris on 19 September 1870'; the contest with the Second Empire (August-September) is the second-french-empire dossier's.

region.text: north-eastern France as the German armies held or fought over it in 1870

ledger.note: December 1870: the Confederation becomes the German Empire. The war goes on ('from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871'); the contest continues in the next pair with the Empire. The pairing here ends with the Confederation.

region.text: north-eastern France

ledger.note: 1871: the government moves to Versailles. 'After the January 1871 surrender', the government 'established a new seat of government at Versailles'; Paris stays the nominal capital (infobox) and the page does not date the return.
January 1871: the war goes on against the German Empire. 'In January 1871, these states became part of the German Empire'; Paris 'fell on 28 January 1871, effectively ending the war'.

region.text: north-eastern France and Paris

ledger.note: 28 January 1871: the armistice. 'On 26 January 1871, the Government of National Defence based in Paris negotiated an armistice' and 'On 28 January, a truce was concluded for 21 days'; the page's infobox ends the war on 28 January 1871.

region.text: north-eastern France and Paris

ledger.note: 1871: German troops stay on French soil as a guarantee. The Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871) 'required military occupation in parts of France until the indemnity was paid' (5,000,000,000 francs in gold, 'one billion in 1871'). The page names no departments; the zone is the growth of Cliopatria's shape from 1871 to 1873 (451 cells), which is wider than a post-treaty garrison (it includes Loiret and the Paris basin) and should be read as the war-time zone.

region.text: the departments held by German troops, from Champagne and Lorraine to the Paris basin and the Loire; the page names none

ledger.note: Late March 1871: the Paris Commune seizes Paris. The page: 'from late March through May 1871' the Commune 'maintained a radical left-wing regime for two months' and was suppressed by the government in May. The Commune held only Paris, so the counterpart is a string (a rebel regime of two months).

region.text: Paris under the Commune

ledger.note: May 1871: the government suppresses the Commune ('suppressed by the government in May'); the page gives 'late March through May 1871'.

region.text: Paris

ledger.note: 10 May 1871: France cedes Alsace-Lorraine. The treaty was 'signed in Frankfurt on 10 May 1871 by the German Empire and the French Third Republic': Alsace (Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin 'except for the city of Belfort and its territory'), 'most of the French department of Moselle', one third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck in Vosges: 1,694 villages and cities, 'about 1,447,000 hectares', 1,597,000 inhabitants. Residents had 'the right of option until 1 October 1872'.

region.text: Alsace-Lorraine: Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin except Belfort, most of Moselle, a third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck (1,694 villages and cities, about 14,470 km2, 1,597,000 inhabitants)

ledger.note: September 1873: the last German troops leave French soil. The indemnity was paid faster than agreed, and German forces withdrew 'in September 1873'. The land of the occupation zone is French in full again.

region.text: the zone held by German troops since 1871

ledger.note: 1885: a protectorate over northern and central Vietnam. 'After the Sino-French War (1884-1885), France took a protectorate over northern and central Vietnam' (the page also says all the colonies were 'acquired during the last two decades of the 19th century'). Indochina's other parts, Tunisia (1881), Madagascar (1896) and Morocco (1912) are not on the page and belong to the colonial dossiers (french-indochina, french-africa, madagascar).

region.text: northern and central Vietnam, the protectorate

ledger.note: Late 1914: Germany occupies the north-east. 'Late 1914: Germany gained military control of important industrial regions in France'; 'The territory occupied by Germany held 64 percent of French pig-iron production'; the First Battle of the Marne (6-12 September 1914) halted the advance; France entered the war on 3 August 1914 (Third Republic page). The page names no departments; the region is the cells that Cliopatria's 1915 shape leaves out (Aisne, Nord, Ardennes, Somme, Pas-de-Calais, Meuse, Oise).

region.text: north-eastern France, the industrial regions held by Germany from late 1914

ledger.note: 5 October 1915: the Army of the Orient lands at Salonika. 'The first troops landed in the port of Salonika on 5 October' under the French general Sarrail; 'In 1915 the French advanced up the Vardar river alone'. The contest is with Bulgaria, which entered the war in October 1915 (principality-of-bulgaria dossier: 'occupation_start 1915-10').

region.text: the Vardar valley and the Bitola basin, where French and Serbian armies fought Bulgarian and German troops

ledger.note: February-April 1917: the Germans fall back to the Hindenburg Line. 'On 25 February the German armies west of the line began Operation Alberich', completed on 5 April, leaving 'a supply desert of scorched earth to be occupied by the entente'. The page lists no regained places; the region is Cliopatria's 1917 growth (11 cells in Oise, Somme and Aisne).

region.text: the ground evacuated in Operation Alberich

ledger.note: Spring 1918: the German offensive retakes ground. The offensive 'very nearly succeeded in driving the entente armies apart, advancing to within shelling distance of Paris for the first time since 1914'. The page gives no date or place; the region is the 20 cells Cliopatria's 1918 shape drops (Somme, Meuse, Aisne, Meurthe-et-Moselle, Oise, Marne).

region.text: the ground lost in the spring offensive

ledger.note: 30 September 1918: the Macedonian front ends. 'The preparatory artillery bombardment began on 14 September. The following day, the French and Serbians attacked'; 'On 29 September, the Bulgarians were granted the Armistice of Salonica by General d'Esperey' and 'The Macedonian front ended at noon on 30 September 1918'.

region.text: the Vardar valley and the Bitola basin

ledger.note: 8 October 1918: French troops land at Beirut. The page: 'On 8 October, French troops disembarked in Beirut' (the sentence gives no year; the context is the end of the war in 1918) and the French occupied the coast 'south to Naqoura (the western zone)', replacing British troops. The region is Cliopatria's Lebanese cells of 1919.

region.text: the coast of Lebanon, 'the western zone'

ledger.note: 17 November 1918: French troops land in Cilicia. 'The first landing took place on 17 November 1918 at Mersin with roughly 15,000 men'; Tarsus was occupied on 19 November. The French army moved 'in accordance with the secret Sykes-Picot Agreement of 1916'. Antep, Marash and Urfa followed 'at the end of 1919', taken over from the British. The region is Cliopatria's Turkish cells of 1919 (Hatay, Adana, Osmaniye, Mersin).

region.text: Cilicia (the Cukurova) and the sanjak of Alexandretta

ledger.note: 11 November 1918: the armistice. 'The Armistice of Compiegne was quickly signed, stopping hostilities on the Western Front on 11 November 1918'; the German armies left the occupied departments within weeks (the page gives no withdrawal dates). The Alsace-Lorraine cells are the next event.

region.text: the occupied north-east

ledger.note: 1 December 1918: the Allies occupy the Rhineland. The occupation ran 'from 1 December 1918 until 30 June 1930'; the French held the Palatinate and the Mainz zone ('the French Eighth Army (Palatinate) and Tenth Army (Mainz) were combined on 21 October 1919 into the French Army of the Rhine'); the Americans handed Koblenz to the French on 27 January 1923. The region copies the weimar-republic dossier's French zone.

region.text: the Koblenz and Mainz zones and the Palatinate, drawn from the growth of Weimar Germany's Cliopatria shape between 1926 and 1930

ledger.note: 28 June 1919: Alsace-Lorraine returns to France. 'France regained Alsace-Lorraine' by the Treaty of Versailles of 28 June 1919. The weimar-republic dossier dates the German loss to the armistice of 11 November 1918 (another page); the Cliopatria shape includes the land from 1919.

region.text: Alsace-Lorraine: Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin except Belfort, most of Moselle, a third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck (1,694 villages and cities, about 14,470 km2, 1,597,000 inhabitants)

ledger.note: January 1920: the French fight the Turkish national forces in Cilicia. 'On 11 February 1920, after 22 days of the Battle of Marash', the French evacuated Marash (so the fighting began about 20 January 1920); Mardin was occupied for one day on 21 November 1919. The war runs 7 December 1918 - 20 October 1921 in the infobox. The counterpart is the Turkish National Movement (no dossier).

region.text: Cilicia and the provinces of Marash, Antep and Urfa

ledger.note: 25 April 1920: France receives the mandate for Syria and Lebanon. 'On 25 April, the Supreme Inter-Allied Council ... granted France the mandate of Syria (including Lebanon)'; General Gouraud 'issued an ultimatum to Faisal' on 14 July and 'captured Damascus with little resistance' on 24 July 1920; 'the State of Greater Lebanon' was proclaimed on 1 September 1920; the League assigned the mandate on 29 September 1923. The year 1920 is the page's context for 25 April.

region.cliopatria: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
region.text: the mandate for Syria and Lebanon

ledger.note: April 1920: the coast of Lebanon passes from military occupation to the mandate (25 April 1920, the grant; Greater Lebanon proclaimed 1 September 1920).

region.text: the coast of Lebanon

ledger.note: 20 October 1921: the Treaty of Ankara. It was 'signed by representatives of the French and the Turks on 20 October 1921, and finalized with Armistice of Mudanya'; a 'Cilicia Peace Treaty' of 9 March 1921 had come first. The sanjak of Alexandretta 'remained under French control' (as part of the mandate).

region.text: Cilicia

ledger.note: 3-7 January 1922: the French leave Cilicia. 'The French forces withdrew from the occupation zone in the first days of 1922'; 'evacuation was completed on 7 January with the last troops leaving Osmaniye'. Cliopatria's shape keeps the cells to 1923.

region.text: Cilicia

ledger.note: 11 January 1923: France and Belgium occupy the Ruhr. 'French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr' on 11 January 1923 (the Third Republic page: when Germany 'fell behind in reparations payments in 1923, France seized the industrialized Ruhr region').

region.text: the Ruhr district, approximate

ledger.note: 25 August 1925: the Ruhr is evacuated. The Dawes Plan 'lowered and restructured Germany's reparations payments, and France agreed to vacate the Ruhr'; the evacuation 'was completed on 25 August 1925'.

region.text: the Ruhr district

ledger.note: 30 June 1930: the Rhineland occupation ends. 'The last of the occupying troops withdrew from the Mainz zone on 30 June 1930'; the Koblenz zone had been evacuated in November 1929.

region.text: the Koblenz and Mainz zones and the Palatinate

ledger.note: June 1940: Germany occupies the north and west. The Battle of France ran from 10 May to 25 June 1940 (infobox) and 'Nazi forces occupied much of France'; the page gives no zone boundaries. The region is France without the Vichy France row's 1940 cells.

region.text: the occupied zone: the north, the Atlantic coast and Alsace-Lorraine

ledger.note: 10 July 1940: the Republic ends; the occupation continues under the successors (nazi-germany and vichy-france dossiers). The pairing closes here only because this state ends.

region.text: the occupied zone

ledger.note: 10 July 1940: the Republic's mandate over Syria and Lebanon passes to Vichy France; the mandate itself ran until 1946 (Mandate page: 'The French mandate lasted until 1946, when French troops finally left Syria and Lebanon').

region.cliopatria: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
region.text: the mandate for Syria and Lebanon

ledger.note: 10 July 1940: the Indochinese protectorates pass to Vichy France (the dossier ends here; the protectorate itself continues under Vichy France, which the french-indochina dossier carries).

region.text: northern and central Vietnam

ledger.note: 10 July 1940: the Third Republic ends. 'until 10 July 1940, after the Fall of France'; 'Vichy France declared: 10 July 1940' (infobox). Its land passes to Vichy France (the unoccupied south) and to the German occupation zone (the north and west).

wars.outcome: German victory: war from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871; France ceded most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine ('as well as most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine'), paid 5 billion francs in gold and endured a German occupation of parts of France until September 1873.
wars.note: The Second Empire's part (Sedan, 2 September 1870) is the second-french-empire dossier's.

wars.name: Paris Commune
wars.outcome: The Commune held Paris 'from late March through May 1871' and was suppressed by the government in May.

wars.name: World War I (Western Front)

zones.text: north-eastern France, held by Germany from late 1914

wars.outcome: Trench warfare from the Swiss frontier to the North Sea; Germany held 64 percent of French pig-iron production in the occupied zone; Operation Alberich (25 February-5 April 1917) and the Armistice of 11 November 1918 returned the ground.

wars.name: Macedonian front
wars.outcome: Armistice of Salonica on 29 September 1918; the front ended at noon on 30 September 1918.

wars.name: Franco-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Ankara, 20 October 1921; the French left Cilicia on 3-7 January 1922; the sanjak of Alexandretta stayed under French control.

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: General Gouraud's ultimatum to Faisal on 14 July 1920; the French won at Maysaloun in less than a day and General Goybet 'captured Damascus with little resistance' on 24 July 1920. The land is the mandate's, not the Republic's.

wars.name: Occupation of the Ruhr
wars.outcome: France and Belgium occupied the Ruhr from 11 January 1923; evacuation completed 25 August 1925 after the Dawes Plan.

wars.name: Battle of France
wars.outcome: 10 May - 25 June 1940; the Republic ended on 10 July 1940 and Vichy France was declared.

certainty.note: The metropolitan frontier is a treaty line, sharp from the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871); the 1870-1873 occupation zone is soft and the Guiana frontiers with Suriname and Brazil are the least sure part of the shape.
The front line moved every month; the metropolitan frontier is unchanged but the held ground (occupation and contest) is soft.
Treaty of Versailles frontier from 28 June 1919; the Rhineland, Ruhr and Cilicia occupation zones are soft, and the 1940 occupation zone has no boundary on the page.

notes: Cliopatria's row 1871-1939 has 14 shapes; the dossier runs 4 September 1870 to 10 July 1940 and adds keyframes 1870 and 1940. Cliopatria draws occupation as ownership throughout and this dossier adjusts every such shape: 1871-72 omits the German-held zone (the German Empire's shape carries it); 1915-1918 omit the German-held north-east; 1919-1930 add the occupied Rhineland, the Saar (League of Nations, not French), Cilicia (to January 1922) and the Lebanese coast (the mandate). Verdict 'adjust' with the 1873 shape (plus Alsace-Lorraine from 1919) as the base. The zones of occupation are Cliopatria's growth, not boundaries given by a page. Disagreement between dossiers: Alsace-Lorraine is dated to 28 June 1919 here (Third Republic page) and to 11 November 1918 in the weimar-republic dossier (another page); a gap-filler should open 'Alsace-Lorraine' or 'Armistice of 11 November 1918'. Counterparts without dossiers: paris-commune (March-May 1871, under a year: string only), turkish-national-movement (Franco-Turkish War, for me-10), kingdom-of-syria (Faisal, 1920, for me-10), saar-basin-territory (1920-1935, flagged by weimar-republic), alsace-lorraine exists. Colonies: only the Vietnam protectorate (1885) and the Syria-Lebanon mandate (1920) are dated by pages opened; Tunisia, Madagascar, Morocco, French West and Equatorial Africa and the Pacific colonies are not on the Third Republic page and belong to their own dossiers (french-africa, madagascar, new-caledonia): the Cliopatria Third Republic shape holds none of them. No rulers strip: the page gives Lebrun (1932-1940) and MacMahon (1873-1879, resigned 30 January 1879) and Grevy, but no full list; List of presidents of France would be the page. Page silent: the area of the French empire per year; the date of the return from Versailles to Paris; the 1940 zone boundary. The French Guiana part of the shape overlaps Suriname (8 cells) and Brazil (3 cells): unverified. Gazetteer: all names are existing countries, admin-1s or places; the lon/lat uses none.
